topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing of complement
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement system and frames its conceptual importance and complexity for the session.

topics.label: Foundations and core biochemistry of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the overall structure, naming conventions, and central biochemical role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the alternative, lectin, and classical recognition pathways that initiate complement and converge to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream immune outcomes of complement activation: opsonization, inflammatory signaling, and membrane attack complex-mediated cell lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the regulatory proteins and molecular mechanisms that protect host tissues from accidental complement-mediated attack.

topics.label: Clinical manifestations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the distinct clinical presentations, infection risks, and autoimmune phenotypes resulting from deficiencies across different complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the mechanisms pathogens employ to resist complement-mediated clearance, highlighting Staphylococcus aureus as a primary model.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the complement lecture and previews the upcoming topic on the adaptive immune system.
